entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The present second application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime no. 57A of 2006, under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 477A, 120B, 34 IPC, P.S. Reoti, District Ballia, with the prayer that in the event of arrest, applicant may be released on bail.

The first anticipatory bail application of applicant was dismissed as not pressed vide order dated 18.01.2023.
3.

It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has an apprehension that he may be arrested in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
It has further been submitted that applicant has no criminal antecedents.

The first information report of this case was lodged in the year 2006 and after investigation charge-sheet Anil Kumar Gupta vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83143569/
1 was submitted in the year 2022.

entities.text: Anil Kumar Gupta vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that 74 persons were named in the first information report.
The allegation that applicant was involved in misappropriation of foodgrains in Scheme of S.G.R.Y during the year 2002-2005, is wholly false.
The applicant was proprietor of Fair Price Shop and there is no specific allegation against him.

It is further submitted that during investigation applicant was granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 26.05.2021 and he has never misused the liberty of bail and thereafter charge-sheet has been submitted.

Similarly placed co-accused Bhagirathi Devi, Kamta Singh, Shanti Devi and Kamlesh Kumar Chauhan have already been granted anticipatory bail by co-ordinate Benches of this Court, copies of which, are available on record.
The applicant undertakes to co-operate during trial and he would appear as and when required by the investigating agency or Court.
It has been stated that in case, the applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate during trial and would obey all conditions of bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the application for anticipatory bail and submitted that there is evidence that applicant was involved in misappropriation of foodgrains.
However, it could not be disputed that similarly placed above-stated co-accused persons have already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court.

5. It may be stated that in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In the instant case, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail,
submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merit of the case, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
7. The instant second anticipatory bail application is hereby allowed.

8. In the event of arrest of the applicant- Anil Kumar Gupta in the aforesaid case crime, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions :-
i.
The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii.The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
iii.The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.
